title: Comparative analysis of pneumothorax diagnosis in X-ray images by trauma surgeons and artificial intelligence
summary:
A traumatic pneumothorax is a potentially life-threatening injury where air enters the space between the lung and the chest wall due to trauma (e.g., an accident). This causes the lung to partially or completely collapse, which can lead to acute shortness of breath. In the emergency room, this injury must therefore be diagnosed extremely quickly and reliably.
Most often, the first diagnostic tool of choice is a conventional chest X-ray (chest radiograph). Since time is critical in hospitals, Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are expected to be used more frequently in the future. These AI systems can automatically scan X-ray images and support the treating physicians in detecting the injury. This could improve the quality of care, especially in time-critical situations or in smaller hospitals.
The study compares the diagnostic accuracy of an already established AI system with that of trauma surgeons (with varying levels of professional experience). The evaluation by experienced radiologists serves as the benchmark ("gold standard").

The central question of the study is: How do the trauma surgeons perform compared to the AI when it comes to correctly identifying a pneumothorax (sensitivity) and classifying healthy patients as healthy (specificity)?
Researchers' assumption (Hypothesis): The AI system has a diagnostic accuracy comparable to the performance of human trauma surgeons.

Further detailed questions:
1. How high is the agreement between the AI system and the perfect benchmark of the radiologists?
2. How high is the agreement between the trauma surgeons' diagnosis and this benchmark?
3. Does the level of professional experience (qualification) of the respective trauma surgeons make a difference?
4. What misclassifications occur?

interventions.name: Retrospective analysis of all adult patients with suspected pneumothorax following preceding thoracic trauma who were treated in the Department of Orthopedics and Trauma Surgery at the BG Klinikum Unfallkrankenhaus Berlin between July 1, 2024, and June 30, 2026.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
-Age ≥ 18 years
-Digitally available conventional chest X-ray in the a.p. view within the examination period, with reporting completed by the AI system
-Treatment at the BG Klinikum Unfallkrankenhaus Berlin
-Chest trauma
-Sufficient image quality
Exclusion criteria:
-Onset of treatment outside the defined inclusion period
-Missing or incomplete radiological report
-Insufficient image quality
-Duplicate or technically uninterpretable datasets
-Age under 18 years
